phases.outcome: Both writers fit a single Goal! call; this omits the dribble and is not a full quality pass.

phases.change: Deliberate perception-only model comparison, identical recorded prompt, sampled frames, output allowance and reasoning effort. No writer rerun or production default change.
phases.outcome: The larger model also falsely labels a goal; no recognition improvement on this clip.

limits: 15 existing development clips; unreviewed sparse labels.
Full-context recorded text planning; not causal live commentary.
Seven historical perception bundles plus eight one-attempt perception fills. Shared perception is identical within each writer pair; no recognition improvement comparison.
Short-clips-v2 removes conflicting long-clip turn quotas and supplies explicit timing budgets after the v1 smoke failure. It is an adapted baseline.
Reviewer disabled; zero provider retries; no paid regression tests.

review.method: Limited source-frame and text review; not an independent blind human study. No model judge used.

findings.critical_failure: Both structurally complete candidates announce a goal that the footage does not establish; independent source inspection shows the keeper continuing play and no goal outcome.
findings.evidence: Local source clip-relative 6, 7, 8, 9 second frames; draft reference also labels a cross/header chance, not a goal.
findings.root_cause: Shared observer hallucinated a confirmed goal and fabricated line/net cue tags. Both writers trusted it.

findings.finding: Both completed outputs correctly call Kane and the low scored penalty. This single short example does not establish useful analyst contribution or general dialogue quality.
One completed candidate correctly says Red card!; the other arm failed. A valid line is not a blind quality win against a missing artifact.

review.acceptance: No whole-suite candidate accepted; unresolved labels and execution/grounding failures remain.

limitations: All 15 clips are development cases with unreviewed sparse labels; related match windows are not independent.
The v2 suite pilot had asymmetric caller uncertainty validation; v4 now applies the same gate to both arms. Do not use v2 completion counts as an architecture superiority comparison.
v3 and v4 are targeted development follow-ups, not held-out improvements or suite reruns.
Both arms returning Goal! in the final dribble check is a timing fit, not complete dribble/shot/goal coverage or useful analysis.

The larger-model vision check used the identical system prompt, source hash/window and sampler parameters. Initial baseline frame hashes were not retained independently; reconstructed frame identity is an inference.
One sample per model/configuration; no general accuracy or statistical significance claim.
Reported cost uses provider token usage and local pricing; not a reconciled invoice. No TTS, fresh research or training.

vision_check.scope: Deliberate perception-only model comparison on one existing failure; not a full-suite quality claim.

larger_model_observations.description: France work the ball along the right edge of the box, playing a grounded pass inward from the touchline area.
A French attacker reaches the byline under pressure from two Jamaica defenders and drives the ball across the face of goal from the right side.
The low cross runs through the crowded six-yard area and the ball crosses the goal line into the left side of the net.

mini_observations.description: A blue-shirted attacker on the right side sends the ball into the penalty area toward a cluster of players.
Near the right edge of the box, the ball is challenged and deflects onward through a crowd of players.
The ball is driven across the face of goal from the right side, skimming through the six-yard area in front of the keeper.
The ball crosses into the left side of the net, with the goalkeeper unable to keep it out.
Players in blue and black converge in the goalmouth after the ball has gone in, while the goalkeeper stands near the line.
